groups.title: Buildings (85)
groups.note: Square, transparent, one building complex on a clean square pad. Lock the look first: make your favourite tier 1 image for one building, then attach it as a reference to every other prompt so the set matches. Do all five tiers of one building together.

groups.title: Building sheet backdrops (17)
groups.note: The wide scenery behind a building on its info sheet. NO building in it: leave an empty flat patch of ground in the lower centre where the game places the building.

groups.title: Troops (16)
groups.note: One unit type per image, transparent, same camera. A squad for infantry and a single vehicle for the rest. Do tier 1 to 4 of a class together and attach tier 1 as a reference.

groups.title: Wall defenses (16)
groups.note: Defensive emplacements that guard your base wall. Transparent, same camera.

groups.title: Heroes (16)
groups.note: Bust portraits with a clean, bright backdrop, no transparency.

groups.title: Map features
groups.note: Sprites for the world map, transparent. REWORKED: each resource has ONE gathering-tile image (the level is a number drawn in code, so the picture never changes with level), and every monster, including one set monster for each gear set, has a loot tile. Old six-level resource pictures are retired. Shown small, so bold shapes and strong colour. The map is made of diamond (isometric) tiles, so every camp, base, citadel and resource site sits on a square patch that reads as a diamond. Nothing is round, hexagonal or octagonal.

groups.title: Holiday monsters, event sets and alliance chests
groups.note: One monster and one loot tile for each of the 15 holidays, one shard for each of the 6 holiday gear sets, plus the alliance gift chest. Holiday monsters use the same pale grey and slate body style, size and camera as the regular monsters with ONE clear festive accent each (colour and prop), so they read as the same creature family. Nothing may show text, numbers, real flags or real logos. Every one must be built so it can be animated later: separate head, body and limbs, and the glowing parts kept as clean separate shapes.

groups.title: Ground tiles (6)
groups.note: Flat, straight top-down textures with NO perspective and NO objects. The game bends them onto the map, so edges must tile seamlessly.

groups.title: Pack banners (22)
groups.note: The big picture at the top of each store pack: a clean, bright loot still life with a colour glow behind it. Rarity colours: 1 green, 2 teal, 3 indigo, 4 magenta, 5 gold.

groups.title: Diamond pile icons (6)
groups.note: Six sizes of diamond pile for the diamond packs, transparent.

groups.title: HUD icons (21)
groups.note: Small glossy icons, front view, transparent. They replace the flat HUD icons wherever the game shows them, so check the HUD looks right after adding them.

groups.title: Hero skill icons (12)
groups.note: Small glossy icons for hero skills and skill tree nodes, front view, transparent, bold shapes that read at 32 pixels.

groups.title: Gear icons (30)
groups.note: Five slots (helmet, armor, footwear, weapon, accessory) in six grades, transparent, front view. Higher grades look grander. Every piece shows exactly ONE round socket position, the same size and a clearly visible spot on every piece (spec of 2026-10-01 18:19: a fully upgraded piece has a single gem socket); it is always drawn as a closed flat brass cap, and the game draws the open ring, the gem and the star glow over it in code. Do a whole slot (six grades) together.

groups.title: Hero XP items (6)
groups.note: Six sizes of XP item, transparent, front view. ALL SIX are the same object (a faceted round medal with a white star on a short ribbon) at growing size and richness, so they read as one family. Do all six together.

groups.title: Crafting materials (6)
groups.note: Six forge materials, one per quality tier, transparent, front view. ALL SIX are the same object (a chunky refined metal ingot bar with a bevelled top) at the same size and angle; only the metal finish and glow change, so they read as one family and can be shown as a 4-to-1 chain. Do all six together. Leave the ingot facets simple and symmetrical so a glint sweep can be animated across the top later.

groups.title: Hero avatars, full body (3)
groups.note: The hero screen centre: a FULL-BODY standing character, front view, identical pose and proportions for every avatar so they can share one animation set (idle breathing, flex, attack). Transparent. Arms slightly away from the body, legs shoulder-width apart, feet flat on an invisible ground, nothing overlapping the silhouette, so the arms, head and torso can be cut out as separate layers and animated later. Same bare/base armour for all three so gear can be drawn on top; avatars differ only in face, hair and base colours.

groups.title: Gear pieces, the full catalog (155)
groups.note: Every piece of the finalized catalog: 13 Basic categories x 5 slots (65), 12 regular sets x 5 (60) and 6 holiday sets x 5 (30). ONE icon per piece, transparent, the identical camera, size, lighting and shape per SLOT across all 155 (the same helmet, vest, rifle, boots and dog-tag amulet silhouette every time), so only the colour scheme and ONE small etched emblem change and a glint or glow can be animated across the same surfaces later. The quality (Grey to Gold) glow, frame and the single gem socket are drawn in code: leave one clear flat spot for the socket in the same place on every piece of a slot. Do a whole set (its 5 slots) together.

groups.title: Named gear materials (60)
groups.note: The named ingredients listed on each gear recipe (Scrap Metal, Apex Beast Hide, Frost-Giant Shards...), one icon each, transparent. ALL share the identical camera, size, lighting and a single chunky raw-chunk silhouette on a small base, so they read as one family; only the material and colour change. The quality tier is NOT drawn (the game shows it with the six ingot tiers). Built to glint or shimmer later.

groups.title: Basic gems (25)
groups.note: The 25 Basic gems that drop from any tile, chest or quest. ALL 25 share the identical stone shape, size, facet layout, camera and lighting (a brilliant-cut stone with a flat octagonal table on a tiny brass setting); only the colour and ONE tiny etched pictogram on the table change, so they read as one family and a glint can sweep across the same facets later. Transparent, centred. The tier 1 to 6 glow ring and pips are drawn in code, so draw one clean stone each.

groups.title: VIP badges (7)
groups.note: One badge family in seven images. Levels 1 and 2 share image 1, levels 3 and 4 share image 2, 5 and 6 share image 3, 7 and 8 share image 4, 9 and 10 share image 5, level 11 has its own (vip_11) and level 12 has one special badge (vip_12). Every badge has the identical shape, size and layout; only the metal and one small detail change, so they read as a set. Attach the first one you like as a reference when making the rest.

groups.title: Avatars and frames (40)
groups.note: Commander avatars are square head-and-shoulders portraits with a plain soft backdrop (the game masks them round). Frames are transparent square borders with the whole inside flat magenta. The 12 hero portraits are reused as avatars, so they are not here.

groups.title: Chat icons and stickers (16)
groups.note: Four channel icons and twelve stickers, transparent, front view, no letters. Stickers are bold expressive emotes in the same glossy style, worn by a small helmeted mascot face or hand.

groups.title: Item icons (18)
groups.note: Icons for pack contents and rewards, transparent, front view, no letters or numbers. Speed-up slips get bigger, brighter and more elaborate with size; hero XP potions grow from a small vial to a huge glowing jug.

groups.title: Tab headers, empty states and mail icons (23)
groups.note: Header banners for the Item, Mail, Alliance, Quest, Event, More, Rewards and Help screens (wide, no lettering, calm middle for a title), eight empty-state pictures shown when a list has nothing in it, and seven mail icons.

groups.title: Alliance art (38)
groups.note: Sixteen alliance emblems, five rank badges, fifteen feature icons (help, tech, gifts, war, territory, shop, members, donations, chat, rally, embassy, throne, mail, quests, flag), a create-alliance banner and the alliance hall backdrop.

groups.title: March and map-action art (20)
groups.note: Two screen headers, ten march-type icons and six small march sprites for the world map (top-down-ish, transparent), plus a route end-marker and a dust puff.

groups.title: Forge rooms, sockets and chests (16)
groups.note: The six Forge room interiors, the socket and star pieces, the blueprint cards and the alliance store and gift chests. Rooms are one building seen from one fixed camera so they read as one set; keep the central third of every room calm for the title. Pieces are transparent and built to be animated later (sockets glow and pulse, stars flare, chests open).

groups.title: Set gems (72)
groups.note: Four gems for each of the 12 weekly monster sets and the 6 holiday sets. ALL 72 share the identical stone shape, size, facet layout, camera and lighting as the Basic gems (a brilliant-cut stone with a flat octagonal table on a tiny brass setting); within a set the four stones share the set colour, and only ONE tiny etched pictogram on the table changes. The fourth gem of every set is its synergy gem: the same stone with a tiny etched four-pointed star. Transparent, centred. The tier 1 to 6 glow ring and pips are drawn in code, so draw one clean stone each.

groups.title: Quest tab art (22)
groups.note: Four quest-list headers, ten quest category icons, four reward chests that grow with rank, and four small status pieces.

groups.title: City backdrop, ground and decor (36)
groups.note: Replaces the flat dark background and square street grid: three full-screen backdrops, ONE background image, a single seamless picture the whole base lies on, a horizon strip, three organic ground islands, three plot pads, six construction-site pieces (scaffold wrap, crane, hanging load, beacon, sparks, dust) that the game animates over a plot being built, four winding road pieces and fourteen scenery pieces that make the base feel like one place.

groups.title: UI parts and effects (24)
groups.note: New in the audit. Reusable interface parts and small effects the game still draws in code. Buttons, frames and bars are text-free and stretch from their middle, so keep the centre plain. Effects are flat 2D, drawn as one separate transparent piece each, because they will be animated later (scaled, faded, spun or looped in code).
